items.title: Growth Accelerations (Hausmann, Pritchett, Rodrik; NBER WP 10566, 2004; JEG 10(4) 2005)
items.excerpt: We look for instances of rapid acceleration in economic growth that are sustained for at least eight years and identify more than 80 such episodes since the 1950s. ... growth accelerations tend to be highly upredictable: the vast majority of growth accelerations are unrelated to standard determinants and most instances of economic reform do not produce growth accelerations.

items.title: The Anatomy of Start-Stop Growth (Jones, Olken; NBER WP 11528, 2005; REStat 90(3) 2008)
items.excerpt: First, all but the very richest countries experience both growth miracles and failures over substantial periods. ... growth accelerations and collapses are asymmetric phenomena. ... despite much talk of poverty traps, even very poor countries regularly grow rapidly
